title: Photosynthetic Response Curves
objective: Interpret leaf light-response curves without treating a short-term single-leaf measurement as a whole-crop yield curve.

terms.definition: Carbon dioxide fixation minus respiratory carbon loss measured over the interval.
Initial efficiency with which absorbed or incident photons increase photosynthesis.
Model-estimated maximum net photosynthetic rate under the measurement conditions.
Relationship between photon flux and measured photosynthetic rate for a defined leaf and environment.

coreScience: A light-response curve measures net leaf gas exchange across a sequence of photon flux levels while other cuvette conditions are controlled. The low-light slope estimates apparent quantum yield; the intercept and curve shape support estimates of dark respiration, compensation, and asymptotic capacity.

Results depend on leaf age, position, acclimation light, cultivar, carbon dioxide, temperature, humidity, nutrition, water status, measurement spectrum, step duration, and model. A leaf may change during the curve, so order, stabilization criteria, leakage checks, and instrument matching matter.

Leaf saturation does not define whole-canopy yield saturation. Increasing top light can send more photons to previously light-limited leaves and inflorescences even when an exposed leaf is near its instantaneous maximum. Cannabis research has directly shown divergence between leaf photosynthetic response and whole-plant inflorescence yield response.
cultivationRelevance: Curves help diagnose acclimation, compare leaves or treatments, and define physiological response under controlled conditions.
Production decisions must combine gas exchange with canopy interception, spatial light distribution, time-integrated photons, carbon allocation, environment, energy, and harvest data.

measureAndRecord.requirement: Cultivar, plant ID, stage, leaf rank, age, orientation, health, and prior light exposure.
CO2, leaf temperature, humidity or VPD, flow, fan, spectrum, and chamber area.
Photon sequence, duration, stabilization rule, repetitions, dark adaptation, and time of day.
Zero and span checks, gasket and leak status, matching, calibration, and excluded points.
Equation, parameter estimates, uncertainty, residual review, and raw observations.

misconceptions: The curve gives the room's best PPFD: It describes a measured leaf under specified short-term conditions.
Amax is a fixed cultivar trait: It changes with acclimation, development, leaf condition, and measurement environment.
Leaf photosynthesis equals yield: Yield integrates canopy capture, respiration, allocation, duration, and losses.
evidenceLimits: Cannabis gas-exchange studies include few genotypes and measurement systems. Model parameters should not be transferred as universal production thresholds.
sourceNotes: Chandra S. et al. (2008). Photosynthetic Response of Cannabis sativa L. to Variations in Photosynthetic Photon Flux Densities, Temperature and CO2 Conditions. Physiology and Molecular Biology of Plants 14:299-306.
